description: Rank invoices by how far their deviation from the overall average invoice unit price exceeds their country's average deviation, and return exactly 10 rows, cutting ties arbitrarily.

a.request: For each invoice, together with its customer's country, compute the average `UnitPrice` of its invoice lines. Take the overall average of these invoice averages, and for each invoice compute its deviation (invoice average minus overall average). Then, for each country, average these deviations over its invoices. For each invoice, show the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and that deviation minus its country's average deviation. Sort by this last value from highest to lowest (blanks last) and return exactly 10 rows, breaking any tie at the cutoff arbitrarily. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country AS Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, avg_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv), cd AS (SELECT dev.*, AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS country_avg_dev FROM dev) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, deviation - country_avg_dev AS deviation_minus_country_avg FROM cd ORDER BY deviation_minus_country_avg IS NULL, deviation_minus_country_avg DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Work out each invoice's average line `UnitPrice` (with its customer's country) and how far that is from the average across all invoices. Which are the top 10 invoices whose deviation sits furthest above their country's average deviation? Show the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and the deviation minus the country's average deviation, sorted highest first (blanks last) and unrounded. Rank invoices by how far their deviation from the overall average invoice unit price exceeds their country's average deviation, and return exactly 10 rows, cutting ties arbitrarily.
c.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, avg_unit_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_unit_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS deviation_minus_country_avg FROM dev ORDER BY deviation_minus_country_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

b.request: Rank invoices by how much each invoice's deviation (its average InvoiceLine UnitPrice minus the overall average of invoice-level average UnitPrices) exceeds the average deviation of invoices in the same customer country, and return exactly 10 rows (invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation, deviation minus country average deviation) sorted descending with NULLs last, unrounded, with ties cut arbitrarily
b.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country AS Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, avg_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv), cd AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS country_avg_dev FROM dev) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, deviation - country_avg_dev AS deviation_minus_country_avg FROM cd ORDER BY deviation_minus_country_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

d.request: For each invoice, compute the average line `UnitPrice` (along with the customer's country) and its deviation from the overall average across all invoices. Then rank invoices by how far that deviation exceeds the average deviation of invoices in the same country (deviation minus country average deviation). Return exactly 10 rows, with ties cut arbitrarily, showing the invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and the deviation minus the country's average deviation. Sort highest first (blanks last), and leave values unrounded.
d.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_unit_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, avg_unit_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_unit_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv), fin AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS dev_minus_country_avg FROM dev) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_unit_price, deviation, dev_minus_country_avg FROM fin ORDER BY dev_minus_country_avg IS NULL, dev_minus_country_avg DESC LIMIT 10
